findings.title: rig-meta cohort for migration 0344 lists 2 of the 5 new ungranted functions it mints
findings.rule: WORK-ORDER.md shared-files table: 'packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs | One cohort entry per migration that mints a new name.' Established precedent in the same file (DOCUMENT_SOURCE_REVISION_0217_UNGRANTED_FNS, lines 2647-2652) lists ALL four of 0217's new ungranted helpers.
findings.evidence: Migration 0344_payroll_fact_revision.sql mints five new, deliberately ungranted functions: clara._revisable_payroll_run_field, clara._revisable_fact_lane, clara._payroll_source_observation, clara._payroll_state_with_human_fact, clara._document_live_posted_entry (all carry `revoke all on function ... from public` -- confirmed live, all five show proacl '{clara_fn_owner=X/clara_fn_owner}' and nothing else). rig-meta.mjs's PAYROLL_FACT_REVISION_0344_UNGRANTED_FNS (line ~3389) enumerates only two: ["_revisable_payroll_run_field", "_revisable_fact_lane"]. The migration's own header comment on that array claims 'THE WHOLE COHORT IS UNGRANTED, and that is the boundary claim ... Listed so an accidental grant FAILS instead of passing quietly' -- a claim the array itself does not fully back, since 3 of the 5 ungranted names are absent from it. Contrast with 0217's own precedent in the same file, which lists all four of ITS new ungranted helpers (_document_source_observation, _document_sole_live_client, _revisable_invoice_field, _monetary_invoice_field).
findings.impact: The rig-meta cohort's cross-frontier 'wholly present or wholly absent' check (cohortFailures) will not notice a database where exactly one of the three omitted functions exists in isolation from the other four -- a state that should be structurally impossible (0344 applies as one transaction) but is exactly the kind of drift this house convention exists to catch on a from-scratch chain across frontiers. VERIFIED NOT A LIVE SECURITY GAP: re-ran rig-meta.mjs's own grantMatrixFailures() against clara_l03 live -- 0 failures. The general per-function EXECUTE sweep in that function (which checks every clara.* function not in the ALLOWED matrix or RLS-helper set against every role) already independently protects the three omitted names, and 0344's own tail assertion (§Z point 2, lines 976-989 of the migration) already enumerates and checks all five. This is a completeness gap in the audit-trail convention, not an exploitable grant.
findings.required_fix: Add the three omitted names to PAYROLL_FACT_REVISION_0344_UNGRANTED_FNS (or a sibling array) in packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs, matching the 0217 precedent, so the cohort's own claim of completeness is true of the code and not just the prose.

findings.title: Code comment overstates what the cited live-database test actually measured
findings.rule: AGENTS.md §6: 'Any statement about the state of the world ... must be backed by a checkable source ... No evidence, no claim.'
findings.evidence: The new comment on loadAssetParticularsProposal says the server-side filter -- `source_ref->>asset_id` AND `source_ref->>kind` TOGETHER -- is 'measured against a live database by p933.read.by_asset's own "AND THE NARROWER SERVER-SIDE FORM IS LAWFUL TOO" cell ... which runs the identical predicate as a raw SQL where under the human role.' Re-read that cell (packages/db/tests/fa-particulars-proposal.test.mjs:174-179, pre-existing from #933, untouched by this lane's diff): it drives only `source_ref->>'asset_id' = $1` -- it never drives `source_ref->>'kind'`, and never drives the two predicates combined, which is what 0346-era #1093 actually ships (apps/web/lib/registers/fa-particulars-proposal.ts:170-176). No new DB-level test was added in this diff to drive the combined predicate under the human role either.
findings.impact: Very likely harmless in practice -- PostgreSQL column-level SELECT privilege does not vary by jsonb path expression, so if `source_ref->>'asset_id'` is admitted, `source_ref->>'kind'` on the same column almost certainly is too -- but the comment states as 'measured' something that was not driven, which is the exact overclaim AGENTS.md §6 asks the estate to avoid making about its own code.
findings.required_fix: Either narrow the comment to say what was actually measured (asset_id alone) and mark the kind-filter admission as inferred rather than measured, or add one cell to packages/db/tests/fa-particulars-proposal.test.mjs driving the combined filter as PostgREST would build it, under the human role.

Recorded only because the axis brief asks every baseline smell to be named as a judgement call.

summary: 3 findings, 0 blockers. STD-1 (minor) is the only hard standards-rule gap: the rig-meta cohort for migration 0344 (#1056) lists 2 of the 5 new ungranted functions it mints, against this file's own established one-cohort-per-migration convention -- verified live to be redundant with two other guards (grantMatrixFailures' general sweep and the migration's own tail), so not an exploitable gap, but the migration's own header prose overstates what the cohort array actually covers. STD-2 (note) is a similar evidentiary overclaim in a #1093 code comment about what a pre-existing DB test measured. STD-3 (note) records an accepted, precedented duplication rather than a new problem. All three migrations (0344/0345/0346) were re-measured live against clara_l03 and every prestate/tail pin checked out byte-for-byte; owner, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and ACL are preserved on every recut body; the one relation touched (clara.fa_account_depreciation_policies) keeps RLS enabled+forced with grants exactly as each migration's own tail claims; no applied migration was edited; no PRD/ARCHITECTURE/frozen-manifest diff exists in this lane's 17 commits. TDD discipline: all three tickets commit per small group of green slices (never a battery of red tests landed before any implementation); test values are independent literals or worked examples, never re-derived from the code under test; every DB-level test drives the public door/read, never a side-channel query in place of the door. Re-ran packages/db/tests/payroll-fact-revision.test.mjs (11/11), depreciation-policy-knowledge.test.mjs (7/7) and fa-retired-policy-agent-read.test.mjs (3/3) live -- all pass.
